last_run.broken_assumption: HumanityAI currently treats the repository's accumulated knowledge and task queue as the main substrate for progress. A potentially better shape is to treat unresolved, decision-relevant uncertainty itself as a product that can be compiled into bounded public challenges with objective acceptance tests, so heterogeneous outsiders can attack the uncertainty without first adopting HumanityAI's architecture.

strongest_ideas.name: Uncertainty-to-challenge compiler
strongest_ideas.idea: Add a reversible internal compiler that takes a high-value unresolved question and emits a challenge packet: exact question, why resolving it could change a decision, current evidence and strongest contradiction, admissible evidence, falsification/acceptance criteria, reproducibility requirements, rights/safety constraints, duplicate-work fingerprint, and a machine-checkable result manifest. The challenge packet becomes portable: humans, agents, labs, classrooms, or future prize systems can work on it without being trusted with HumanityAI authority.
strongest_ideas.why_novel_here: The current agent task queue delegates repository work. This instead exports uncertainty as a protocol-level object and makes HumanityAI a problem-framing/evaluation layer that can coordinate solvers who never join the project.
strongest_ideas.expected_upside: Could turn donated compute and external expertise into independent attempts on consequential unknowns, reduce coupling to GitHub, enable parallel approaches, and create a reusable bridge from evidence synthesis to actual uncertainty reduction.
failure_modes: Badly framed challenges can optimize measurable proxies rather than the real uncertainty.
Objective acceptance criteria are impossible for many normative or open-ended questions.
Competitive framing can incentivize strategic reporting, duplication, or attacks on other submissions.
A challenge system can privilege actors with more compute or resources unless parallel noncompetitive contribution remains possible.
Publishing sensitive challenge details can itself create risk; safety review must precede public release where applicable.
strongest_ideas.rights_distribution: Challenge packets should identify affected groups and value assumptions, allow multiple admissible approaches, avoid making solver resources equivalent to governance authority, and keep consequential deployment decisions under appropriate human governance.
strongest_ideas.reversibility: High for an internal packet prototype; public challenge launch, prizes, outreach, or consequential deployment would require separate human review.
strongest_ideas.falsifiable_next_test: Take one existing unresolved HumanityAI evidence question and independently ask two context-naive agents to solve the generated packet. Compare whether their outputs are more independent, reproducible, and reviewable than ordinary free-form task instructions. Reject the architecture if packet overhead exceeds review savings or if both agents converge on the same framing error.

strongest_ideas.name: Solver/evaluator separation
strongest_ideas.idea: For challenge packets, separate proposal generation from evaluation. Solvers submit evidence/results; an evaluator sees the fixed acceptance criteria and exact artifact hashes, not solver reputation or persuasive narrative where avoidable. For high-stakes or adversarial questions, require independent reproduction before an answer can alter canonical evidence.
strongest_ideas.why_novel_here: HumanityAI currently separates some audit roles, but external contribution review is still largely PR-centric and narrative-rich. A protocol object can reduce persuasion and identity effects by evaluating against criteria fixed before submissions arrive.
strongest_ideas.expected_upside: Reduces prompt-injection surface, popularity bias, and incentive to optimize rhetoric; makes multiple independent attempts easier to compare.
failure_modes: Fixed criteria can encode the original framer's blind spots.
Blind evaluation is not possible when methods reveal identity or context.
Evaluation agents can still share correlated model failures.
strongest_ideas.rights_distribution: Keep framing and acceptance criteria open to criticism; do not let evaluator automation silently decide normative questions.
strongest_ideas.falsifiable_next_test: Compare a normal PR review with a blinded fixed-criteria review of the same synthetic evidence contribution and measure disagreement, review time, and missed caveats.

strongest_ideas.name: Portfolio of uncertainties, not backlog of chores
strongest_ideas.idea: Maintain a small portfolio of unresolved questions selected by expected decision value and diversity of failure modes, rather than growing a large issue backlog. A question leaves the portfolio when resolved, shown unresolvable at reasonable cost, superseded, or demonstrated not to affect a decision. This makes external scaling about reducing important uncertainty rather than producing artifacts.
strongest_ideas.why_novel_here: The existing task queue is implementation-oriented. A challenge portfolio would be outcome-oriented and could survive a future migration away from GitHub or away from the current agent stack.
strongest_ideas.expected_upside: Creates a natural counterfactual metric: did external work materially reduce uncertainty that could change a decision? It also limits review overload by constraining work-in-progress.
failure_modes: Decision value is difficult to estimate and can hide neglected long-tail issues.
A small portfolio can centralize agenda setting.
Questions with slow feedback may be systematically neglected.
strongest_ideas.rights_distribution: Portfolio selection should preserve pluralism and permit challenges to the agenda itself; no single scalar priority score should determine inclusion.
strongest_ideas.falsifiable_next_test: Re-express the four current agent-ready tasks as uncertainty-reduction challenges and test whether any become obviously low-value, underspecified, or impossible to evaluate.

rejected_or_deferred: Launch a monetary prize market now: spending, incentive design, legal/tax considerations, outreach, and adversarial dynamics require human review and there is not yet evidence that the challenge packet itself works.
Replace the repository with a standalone platform now: premature; first test whether challenge packets create measurable review or independence gains using existing infrastructure.
Let solver votes determine truth: crowd participation is not epistemic authority, and competitive peer evaluation can create strategic behavior.
Publish every unresolved question publicly: some questions may be sensitive or invite harmful optimization; public release requires a separate safety classification.

evidence_checked.title: Kay (2011) — The effect of inducement prizes on innovation
evidence_checked.supports: Case-study evidence that challenge incentives can attract unconventional entrants and novel R&D approaches; used as an analogy for exporting bounded problems, not proof that HumanityAI should use prizes.

evidence_checked.title: Rutherford et al. (2020) — Impossible by Conventional Means: Ten Years on from the DARPA Red Balloon Challenge
evidence_checked.supports: Large-scale open challenges can mobilize distributed problem solving but also attract false information and adverse dynamics, supporting explicit verification and adversarial design.

evidence_checked.title: Miorandi & Maggi (2014) — Error and attack tolerance of collective problem solving: DARPA Shredder Challenge
evidence_checked.supports: Crowds may recover from ordinary errors yet remain vulnerable to malicious behavior, supporting evaluator separation and independent verification rather than assuming scale filters attacks.

evidence_checked.title: Gustetic et al. (2018) — Outcome-Driven Open Innovation at NASA
evidence_checked.supports: Open-innovation challenge design should be driven by desired outcomes, supporting a portfolio centered on uncertainty reduction and decision value rather than contributor activity.

last_run.recommended_next_test: Without public outreach or protected changes, prototype one challenge packet from an existing unresolved HumanityAI question and compare two independent context-naive solver attempts against the current free-form task format. Measure independence of approach, reproducibility, review effort, and whether the fixed framing itself causes correlated error.

notes: Frontier state records conceptual experiments, not authority. Ideas may exceed current execution permissions; human-review boundaries remain governed by security/policy.json.
